metadata.title: PIRLS 2011 Encyclopedia: Education Policy and Curriculum in Reading (Volume 1: A–K)
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center, Lynch School of Education, Boston College

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This PIRLS 2011 Encyclopedia volume is a curriculum/policy compendium rather than an empirical student-level modeling paper. It describes intended curriculum, instructional approaches, and system context for PIRLS 2011 and prePIRLS participants, drawing on country questionnaire information and qualitative chapter syntheses. The text reports that PIRLS 2011 used nationally representative samples of approximately 4,000 students from 150–200 schools per country, but it does not specify the analyst-facing weight variables (e.g., student/sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures. For any secondary quantitative analyses using PIRLS microdata, analysts should apply the PIRLS complex survey design weights provided in the international database; however, this encyclopedia chapter text does not document those weight variable names or their use in estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This encyclopedia is not an empirical predictive/analytic study of student achievement outcomes using PV-based scores; it is a qualitative and policy-oriented reference describing education systems and reading curricula. Because no PV-based dependent variable is modeled here, plausible values handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is also not reported because the excerpted content does not present an estimation model with an analytic dataset and missingness procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The excerpted encyclopedia introduction states that PIRLS 2011 used nationally representative samples of approximately 4,000 students from 150–200 schools per participating country, and that approximately 325,000 students participated in total across PIRLS 2011, benchmarking, and prePIRLS. No analytic subsample definition, grade restriction, or exclusion rule is provided in the provided text for this encyclopedia volume; the chapters are prepared from each country’s viewpoint and are not described as a single pooled student-level analytic dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2011 Encyclopedia volume is a policy and curriculum reference that complements the PIRLS 2011 International Results in Reading report. It describes the intended curriculum (official reading curriculum goals, instructional approaches, teacher preparation requirements, and assessment/monitoring practices) for PIRLS 2011 participants and prePIRLS benchmarking participants, using country questionnaire information and expert chapter syntheses. The introduction reports that PIRLS 2011 was conducted at five-year intervals and assessed reading achievement after four years of schooling, with nationally representative samples of about 4,000 students from 150–200 schools per country and approximately 325,000 students in total across PIRLS 2011, benchmarking, and prePIRLS. The excerpt does not present student-level predictive modeling, PV-based outcome estimation, or reported ML performance metrics. Therefore, no quantitative benchmark effects are extracted from this text; the main contribution is contextual interpretation to support cross-country comparisons of reading policy and practice.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a curriculum/policy encyclopedia introduction rather than an empirical ML paper. The provided text does not specify an analytic dataset, PV or achievement outcome modeling, missing-data strategy, or any ML algorithms with performance metrics, so the extraction is necessarily sparse on modeling fields. The study’s purpose is descriptive and comparative (intended curriculum and system context), which explains why main_findings and confounders_identified are empty.
